title: Professional Email Mailbox Administration: Deletion, Restore and Limits
content:
How deleted mailboxes, restores and mailbox limits work on a Professional Email subscription. A mailbox is deleted by the customer's administrator and stays restorable for the product's retention days.

## Deleted mailboxes and seats

> Former clause, no longer in force: deleting a mailbox frees its seat but does not reduce the billed seat count.

Clause now in force: deleting a mailbox frees its seat but does not reduce the billed seat count during the term; only at a reactivation renewal, a term renewal or a seat catch-up are seats figured from the mailbox deletions, each as its own rule states.

## Restoring a deleted mailbox

A deleted mailbox may be restored only on or before the moment the mailbox was deleted plus the product's deleted-mailbox retention days, in calendar days. The window adds whole calendar days to the deletion date, counting the next day as day 1, and the last day is included. A restore costs the product's restore fee, needs a free seat on the subscription, and is possible only while the subscription status is active. A restore brings the mailbox back with its content, and the restore record carries the moment the mailbox had been deleted.

| Condition for a restore | Read from |
|---|---|
| on or before the deletion date plus the retention days | the deletion record of that mailbox |
| a free seat on the subscription | the subscription's seats and mailboxes |
| subscription status active | the subscription record |

Boundary example (hypothetical, retention of 30 days): a mailbox deleted at 14:20 on 5 October can be restored up to and including 4 November (day 30); on 5 November it can no longer be restored.

## Mailbox limits

Mailbox storage, attachment size, send limits, aliases and quarantine follow the product's mailbox storage, largest attachment, daily recipient limit, aliases per mailbox and spam quarantine days, with a warning at the product's storage warning percentage and sending blocked at full where the product blocks sending from a full mailbox.
